body.prompt:
I'm making concept art for a cooperative board game called Stewards of the Long Voyage: Great Houses steward a vast generation ship; generations of leaders rise and retire. Style: RETRO SPACE — a 1950s pulp science-fiction paperback cover come to life. Gouache painting with flat colour and soft painted gradients, halftone-dot shading, chunky outlines, chrome highlights, rocket fins, atomic starbursts, ringed planets, mid-century modern interiors, a cheerful key light. People are sincere, not parody; the stakes are real. Palette: deep teal (#0F3A48), turquoise (#3AB0A8), tangerine (#E8603A), mustard gold (#F6C85A), cream (#FBEFD6), pink (#E88AA0), lime (#A8C860). Never put any text, letters, logos, borders or watermarks in the images.

Tall portrait image, exactly the layout of the attached guide. Repaint the guide as a finished, empty trading-card frame for this game, flat and straight-on like a printed card template, quiet enough that hundreds of these on a table look calm. Keep every shape exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is: the thin name bar at the top; the narrow column down the left edge with its eight round sockets stacked top to bottom; the arched portrait window beside it (straight sides, a gently rounded arch on top, a flat foot); the text panel below the window; and the large rounded Legacy plaque across the bottom. The arch window and the Legacy plaque stay perfectly flat, empty deep teal (#0F3A48); the name bar, text panel, column and its eight sockets stay plain, empty cream. Paint only the frame around them: a cream card border with a very fine halftone texture, a slim brushed-chrome bezel tracing the arch window, the column and the Legacy plaque, a thin deep-teal keyline inside the card edge, and one small tangerine atomic starburst as the only accent, centred just above the Legacy plaque. No text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks.

Very wide landscape image, exactly the layout of the attached guide, with the panel filling the whole frame edge to edge. Repaint the guide as one panel of the Wall of Leaders as a quiet gallery of ancestors in a mid-century science museum, flat and straight-on like a board-game component. Keep every shape exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is: four identical wide arched windows in a row (straight sides, a gently rounded arch on top, a flat foot), a rounded plaque window under each, and a small round thumb notch at the top edge above each arch. The windows, plaques and notches stay perfectly flat, empty deep teal (#0F3A48), with nothing inside them. Paint only the wall around them: warm ivory plaster with a soft painted texture, a low deep-teal wainscot along the bottom with one thin atomic pinstripe, a slim brushed-chrome frame tracing each arch, a brass placard frame tracing each plaque, a small brass picture light above each arch casting a gentle pool of light, and a small blank engraved brass disc centred under each plaque for the slot number. Calm, dignified, museum-quiet; no starbursts, no orange, no planets. No text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks.
